title: Local epidemiology and resistance profiles in acute uncomplicated cystitis (AUC) in women: a prospective cohort study in an urban urological ambulatory setting (Seitz et al., BMC Infect Dis. 2017)

claims.text: E. coli is by far the most common uropathogen in acute uncomplicated cystitis in women, found in more than 80% of positive urine cultures.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli (E. coli) is still by far the most common uropathogen for acute uncomplicated cystitis (AUC) in women and is found in more than 80% of the positive urine cultures.

claims.text: In this cohort the most common organism was E. coli at 86.3% (365/423), followed by Enterococcus faecalis 10.2% (43/423) and Klebsiella pneumoniae 3.5% (15/423).
claims.byte_quote: The most common bacteria was E. coli with 86.3% (365/423) followed by Enterococcus faecalis with 10.2% (43/423) and Klebsiella pneumoniae with 3.5% (15/423).

claims.text: Summary organism distribution: E. coli 86%, Enterococcus faecalis 10%, Klebsiella pneumoniae 4%.
claims.byte_quote: The most commonly detected bacteria was E. coli with 86%, followed by Enterococcus faecalis with 10% and Klebsiella pneumoniae with 4%.

claims.text: E. coli was highly susceptible to fosfomycin-trometamol (99.2%), nitrofurantoin (98.1%) and cefpodoxime (92.9%).
claims.byte_quote: Susceptibility testing showed E. coli strains to be highly sensitive to the following oral antibiotics: fosfomycin-trometamol (99.2%), nitrofurantoin (98.1%) and cefpodoxime (92.9%).

claims.text: E. coli resistance: ciprofloxacin 15.1%, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 25.2%, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 25.2%.
claims.byte_quote: E. coli was resistant to ciprofloxacin in 15.1% of cases, to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in 25.2% of cases and to amoxicillin/clavulanic acid in 25.2% of cases.

claims.text: E. coli aminopenicillin resistance was alarming, between 25.2% and 39.7% (ampicillin, amoxicillin with sulbactam/clavulanic acid).
claims.byte_quote: Our data demonstrate alarming resistance rates for aminopenicillins (ampicillin, amoxicillin in combination with sulbactam and clavulanic acid, respectively) between 25.2 and 39.7%.

claims.text: Fosfomycin, pivmecillinam and nitrofurantoin are first-line therapy with high evidence level (LE 1a, GR A).
claims.byte_quote: Fosfomycin, pivmecilliam and nitrofurantoin are considered to be first-line therapy with high levels of evidence (LE: 1a, GR: A).

claims.text: An antibiotic resistance rate below 20% suffices to classify an agent as first-line medication.
claims.byte_quote: Resistance rates of <20% already suffice to class an antibiotic as first-line medication.

claims.text: Fosfomycin-trometamol and nitrofurantoin can be given as first-line therapy without susceptibility testing.
claims.byte_quote: On the basis of our data and international studies (ECO-SENS) it can currently be confirmed that fosfomycin-trometamol and nitrofurantoin can be given in our urological practice as first-line therapy without susceptibility testing.

claims.text: TRS, CIP and AMC should only be used to treat AUC after a susceptibility test has been performed.
claims.byte_quote: AUC should therefore only be treated with TRS, CIP and AMC after a susceptibility test has been carried out.

claims.text: Mean patient age was 32.7 years (range 18-65), with the age peak at 18-25 years (42%).
claims.byte_quote: The average age of the patients was 32.7 years (range 18–65). The age peak in the cohort was between ages 18 and 25 (42%).

claims.text: AUC was more common in pre-menopausal than post-menopausal women (86.9% vs 13.1%).
claims.byte_quote: Among pre-menopausal patients AUC was more common than among post-menopausal women (86.9% vs. 13.1%).

claims.text: Three main risk factors influencing AUC rate: recurrent UTIs (20.3%), preceding sexual intercourse (15.3%), and a new sex partner (12.9%).
claims.byte_quote: Three main factors that might influence the rate of AUC in our cohort were recurrent urinary tract infections (20.3%), preceding sexual intercourse (15.3%) and a new sex partner (12.9%).

claims.text: AUC was defined by at least one of: suprapubic pain, urge symptoms, dysuria, increased voiding frequency.
claims.byte_quote: Indicators of an AUC were defined in terms of at least one of the following symptoms: suprapubic pain, urge symptoms, dysuria and increased voiding frequency.

claims.text: A urine culture was defined as positive at >=10e3 CFU/mL; mixed cultures were not analysed.
claims.byte_quote: A urine culture was defined as positive if ≥10e3CFU/mL. Mixed cultures were not analysed.
